title: Momentum
keyIdea: Momentum is mass times velocity: p = m × v, measured in kg m/s. Because velocity has a direction, momentum is a vector: choose one direction as positive and anything moving the other way has negative momentum. A heavy, slow object can have more momentum than a light, fast one.
familyTip: Compare a slow shopping trolley full of bottles with an empty one pushed at the same speed: which is harder to stop? Then ask which has more momentum: a 2000 kg van at 5 m/s or a 70 kg cyclist at 10 m/s, and work it out with p = m × v.

visual.caption: Slide the mass and the velocity. The formula p = m × v gives the momentum in kg m/s.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag velocity arrows and watch signed momentum bars: match a target, slow a truck to a cyclist's momentum, reverse a cart, double a speed.

kid: Momentum tells you how much motion something has. It depends on two things: how much mass it has and how fast it is moving. The rule is p = m × v.
Use mass in kilograms and velocity in metres per second. Then the unit of momentum is kg m/s. A 2 kg cart at 6 m/s has 2 × 6 = 12 kg m/s.
Mass matters as much as speed. A 2000 kg truck at 5 m/s has 10 000 kg m/s. A 70 kg cyclist at 10 m/s has only 700 kg m/s, even though the cyclist is faster.

Momentum has a direction. Pick right as positive. A cart moving left has a negative velocity, so its momentum is negative too. Two equal carts moving apart at the same speed have a total momentum of zero.
adult: Ages 14 to 16. GCSE physics (AQA 4.5.7.1, higher tier): momentum is defined by p = m v, with p in kg m/s, m in kg and v in m/s. NGSS HS-PS2-2 builds on this to show that total momentum is conserved when no outside force acts.

Momentum is a vector, so its sign shows direction. Because p is proportional to v, doubling the speed doubles the momentum. Kinetic energy, ½ m v², is the quantity that goes up four times. Momentum is the base for the next topics: conservation of momentum in collisions, and impulse, F Δt = Δp.

Common mistakes: adding mass and velocity instead of multiplying; using grams without converting (500 g gives a value 1000 times too big); dropping the minus sign for motion in the negative direction; mixing up momentum with kinetic energy or giving it in joules; and assuming the faster object always has more momentum.

In the lab you drag velocity arrows and watch signed momentum bars. You match a target value, slow a truck until it matches a cyclist, reverse a cart to make the total zero, double a speed, and convert grams before multiplying.

practice.prompt: A {m} kg trolley moves at {v} m/s. What is its momentum in kg m/s?
practice.hint: Use p = m × v with mass in kg and velocity in m/s.

practice.prompt: Which has more momentum: a 2000 kg truck at 5 m/s or a 70 kg cyclist at 10 m/s?
practice.hint: Work out m × v for each one. Do not just compare the speeds.
practice.explain: Truck: 2000 × 5 = 10 000 kg m/s. Cyclist: 70 × 10 = 700 kg m/s. The truck has far more.

practice.prompt: A {m} kg cart moves left at {v} m/s. Taking right as positive, what is its momentum in kg m/s?
practice.hint: Moving left means the velocity is negative. Keep the sign in p = m × v.

practice.prompt: A ball of mass 500 g moves at 4 m/s. What is its momentum?
practice.hint: Change grams to kilograms first: 500 g = 0.5 kg.
practice.explain: p = 0.5 × 4 = 2 kg m/s. Using 500 would make it 1000 times too big, and J is the unit of energy.

practice.prompt: A cart's speed doubles while its mass stays the same. What happens to its momentum?
practice.hint: p = m × v: what happens to the product when one factor doubles?
practice.explain: p is proportional to v, so p doubles. Kinetic energy (½mv²) is the one that goes up 4 times.

pool.prompt: A {m} kg car moves at {v} m/s. Find its momentum in kg m/s.
pool.hint: Multiply the mass in kg by the velocity in m/s.

pool.prompt: An object has momentum {p} kg m/s and mass 2 kg. What is its velocity in m/s?
pool.hint: Rearrange p = m × v to v = p ÷ m.

pool.prompt: What is the unit of momentum?
pool.hint: Multiply the unit of mass by the unit of velocity.
pool.explain: kg × m/s = kg m/s. The joule is for energy and the newton is for force.

pool.prompt: Two 1 kg carts move apart, one at +3 m/s and one at −3 m/s. What is their total momentum?
pool.hint: Momentum is a vector. Add the two values with their signs.

pool.prompt: Ali says a 60 kg runner at 7 m/s has 67 kg m/s of momentum. What did he do wrong?
pool.hint: Look at how 67 can be made from 60 and 7.

pool.prompt: A 0.16 kg cricket ball at 40 m/s and a 70 kg person walking at 1.5 m/s. Which has more momentum?
pool.hint: Find m × v for each: 0.16 × 40 and 70 × 1.5.
pool.explain: Ball: 6.4 kg m/s. Person: 105 kg m/s. The slow but heavy person has more.

pool.prompt: Why is momentum a vector but speed is not?
choices: It uses velocity, which has a direction
It uses mass, which has a direction
Because it is measured in kg m/s
pool.hint: Which part of p = m × v carries a direction?
pool.explain: Mass has no direction; velocity does. So p = m × v has the direction of the velocity.

pool.prompt: A 2 kg cart at 3 m/s speeds up to 6 m/s. What is its new momentum?
pool.hint: Work out p = m × v with the new velocity.
pool.explain: 2 × 6 = 12 kg m/s, double the old 6 kg m/s.
